subject: MAP & Eval Milestones — pricing, true-up and contract redlines
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@datwave.com>
Cc: Elise Wong <elise@datwave.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Initial MAP + Eval proposal for DataWave POC

Hi Samir / Elise —

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. Per our call I attached a working MAP (MAP_v3.xlsx) and a short SOW draft that aligns milestones to commercial milestones. High-level ask: can you confirm timing for the 6‑week eval (start date window) and the target ramp over months 1–6 so we can lock pricing/commit tiers?

Key commercial points we proposed in the MAP:
- Eval: 6 weeks, success metric = 95th percentile inference latency under 350ms on representative workload + sample quality acceptance test set.
- Month 1 ramp commit: 50k inference tokens/day (baseline), month 6: 1.5M tokens/day — staged commit with quarterly true-up.
- Pricing tiers: base unit price for text generation tokens, embedding units priced separately; milestone-based discounts: 10% at ARR > $200k, additional 5% at ARR > $500k.
- True-up cadence: quarterly (customer pays delta above committed usage; vendor credits if usage below committed?).
- Price protection: proposed 180 days from execution.

Open items we need your feedback on:
1) Does quarterly true-up cadence work for procurement / finance?
2) Is the definition of "billable unit" (we're using tokens produced + embedding calls) acceptable or do you need a different metric (requests per minute, model-input tokens, output tokens)?
3) Any constraints on price protection or commit ramp that would affect acceptance?

I copied our AE, Marissa, and Neha from sales ops so we can move quickly. If the MAP looks reasonable, we can schedule a 30‑min redline session with legal to capture must-have contract changes.

Thanks —
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: MAP_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet), SOW_Draft.pdf (doc)

From: Samir Patel <samir@datwave.com>

Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial MAP + Eval proposal for DataWave POC

Marcus —

Thanks for the package. We reviewed the MAP and have a few concerns we need addressed before allocating headcount for the eval and moving the legal queue:

1) True-up cadence: quarterly is OK operationally, but finance will not accept unlimited lookbacks. We require a cap (we typically accept 120% annual true-up max) and an ability to amortize over the quarter.
2) Price protection: 180 days is short for our procurement cycles. Can you extend to 12 months for lock-in on unit price following signature?
3) Definition of usage: we bill internally by API calls + compute minutes. We need a clearer mapping between your "tokens" metric and our billing units; ambiguous definitions create reconciliation risk.
4) Ramp & discounts: the proposed tier thresholds are fine, but procurement asks that discounts be tied to committed ARR rather than observed usage during the MAP.

Attached are two items from our side: a short procurement checklist and internal timing constraints. We can jump on a call Wednesday afternoon.

- Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Platform Engineering, DataWave
Attachments: DW_procurement_checklist.pdf

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Initial MAP + Eval proposal for DataWave POC — procurement asks

Marcus / team —

Thanks for the context and draft redlines. I reviewed Samir's procurement asks and sketched defensive language. Summary of our recommended positions (high level):

1) True-up cap: accept customer's request for an annual cap on retrospective true-ups but propose 150% (not 120%) as a compromise if they want more flexibility during the first 12 months of production. Rationale: avoids underpayment risk while still providing a guardrail.

2) Lookback window & reconciliation: offer a 2-quarter lookback for reconciliation, with invoicing within 45 days after quarter close and dispute window of 60 days. We should avoid unlimited lookbacks and clearly exclude historical billing under prior pricing.

3) Price protection: recommend a 9‑month standard price protection period from effective date. We can extend to 12 months if DataWave commits to an ARR threshold (e.g., $250k). If client requests unilateral 12 months without a commit, we decline.

4) Definition of billable unit: propose a two-component definition: (a) model input tokens + model output tokens measured at the system boundary and (b) embedding calls counted per request. We will publish the measurement spec as a schedule to the agreement. Additionally, provide a mapping worksheet during the MAP to reconcile their "compute minutes" metric to our tokens metric.

5) Discounts and commit linkage: discounts are only applied to committed ARR. MAP-observed usage can trigger credits but not permanent discount re-pricing unless a signed amendment increases committed ARR.

I added exact redline language into Redlines_0619.docx and highlighted fallback positions. My suggested concession to push deal: offer a one-time ramp credit (10% credit on month 1 usage if they sign within 30 days) in exchange for a 12‑month commit at $250k ARR.

If you want, I'll join the call with Samir on Wednesday to run through the redlines.

- Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachment: Redlines_0619.docx (updated comments)

Appreciate the quick feedback and the checklist you sent. Following internal discussions (summary below), here's what we can bring to the table to keep momentum and protect both parties' economics:

Proposed commercial updates (redline highlights attached):
- True-up cadence: quarterly reconciliation remains. We will accept an annual cap but propose 150% for the first 12 months, with a commitment to revisit after year one. Aim: limit surprise credits while giving your finance predictability.
- Lookback & invoicing: 2-quarter reconciliation lookback, invoices issued within 45 days after quarter close; 60-day dispute window.
- Price protection: standard 9 months from execution. If DataWave signs a minimum $250k ARR commit within 30 days, we'll extend to 12 months.
- Billable unit definition: tokens = input tokens + output tokens measured at the API edge; embeddings counted per call. We attached a mapping worksheet in MAP_v3.xlsx that translates sample compute-minute metrics to tokens for reconciliation.
- Ramp concession: one-time 10% usage credit for month 1 if signature occurs within 30 days (to de-risk your ramp).
- Discounts: discounts apply to committed ARR only. MAP usage can create credits but not change committed pricing tiers without an amendment.

Next steps:
1) Laura and I will join a 30‑min call with you Wednesday 21 Jul 10am PT to walk through the redlines. Please confirm or propose an alternate time.
2) Procurement: if the $250k ARR extension to 12 months is acceptable in principle, we'll draft the amendment language today and circulate.
3) Legal: final redlines will be sent as a tracked doc (Redlines_0619.docx).

I've attached the updated redlines and MAP. If this alignment looks acceptable, we can lock the eval start window for the week of Aug 3 and secure engineering seats.

Thanks —
